21913-the-talking-leaves-an-indian-story.title: An Indian Story
21913-the-talking-leaves-an-indian-story.creator: William O. Stoddard
21913-the-talking-leaves-an-indian-story.description: A book by William O. Stoddard. was that excited crowd of men down there in the valley. The air was so clear, and the light so brilliant among those snow-capped mountain ranges, that even things far off seemed sometimes close at hand.

arxiv-2304-01613.title: Distributed Block Coordinate Moving Horizon Estimation for 2D Visual-Inertial-Odometry SLAM
arxiv-2304-01613.creator: Emilien Flayac, Iman Shames
arxiv-2304-01613.description: Abstract This paper presents a Visual Inertial Odometry Landmark-based Simultaneous Localisation and Mapping algorithm based on a distributed block coordinate nonlinear Moving Horizon Estimation scheme. The main advantage of the proposed method is that the updates on the position of the landmarks are based on a Bundle Adjustment technique that can be parallelised over the landmarks.

arxiv-2308-01455.title: Coarse-grained simulations of DNA and RNA systems with oxDNA and oxRNA models: Introductory tutorial
arxiv-2308-01455.creator: Michael Matthies, Matthew L. Sample, Petr Šulc
arxiv-2308-01455.description: Abstract ABSTRACT We present a tutorial on setting-up the oxDNA coarse-grained model for simulations of DNA and RNA nanotechnology. The model is a popular tool used both by theorists and experimentalists to simulate nucleic acid systems both in biology and nanotechnology settings. The tutorial is aimed at new users asking "Where should I start if I want to use oxDNA".

arxiv-2310-02080.title: Design Considerations for a Phase II platform trial in Major Depressive Disorder
arxiv-2310-02080.creator: Michaela Maria Freitag, Dario Zocholl, Elias Laurin Meyer, Stefan M. Gold, Marta Bofill Roig, Heidi De Smedt, Martin Posch, Franz König, on behalf of the EU-PEARL MDD Investigators
arxiv-2310-02080.description: Abstract 1 Abstract Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is one of the most common causes of disability worldwide. Unfortunately, about one-third of patients do not benefit sufficiently from available treatments and not many new drugs have been developed in this area in recent years. We thus need better and faster ways to evaluate many different treatment options quickly.

arxiv-2402-01274.title: On the Transferability of Large-Scale Self-Supervision to Few-Shot Audio Classification
arxiv-2402-01274.creator: Calum Heggan, Sam Budgett, Tim Hospedales, Mehrdad Yaghoobi
arxiv-2402-01274.description: Abstract In recent years, self-supervised learning has excelled for its capacity to learn robust feature representations from unlabelled data. Networks pretrained through self-supervision serve as effective feature extractors for downstream tasks, including Few-Shot Learning. While the evaluation of unsupervised approaches for few-shot learning is well-established in imagery, it is notably absent in acoustics.

arxiv-2403-18880.title: On Unitification of ∗ * -rings
arxiv-2403-18880.creator: Sanjay More, Anil Khairnar and B. N. Waphare
arxiv-2403-18880.description: Abstract 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 16W10; Secondary 16D25 Abstract: S. K. Berberian raised the open problem “Can every weakly Rickart * -ring be embedded in a Rickart * -ring? with preservation of right projections?” Berberian has given a partial solution to this problem. Khairnar and Waphare raised a similar problem for p.q.-Baer * -rings and gave a partial solution.

arxiv-2406-17637.title: Nowcasting in triple-system estimation
arxiv-2406-17637.creator: Daan B. Zult, Peter G. M. van der Heijden, Bart F. M. Bakker
arxiv-2406-17637.description: Abstract Multiple systems estimation uses samples that each cover part of a population to obtain a total population size estimate. Ideally, all the available samples are used, but if some samples are available (much) later, one may use only the samples that are available early.

arxiv-2502-11061.title: Déjà Vu? Decoding Repeated Reading from Eye Movements
arxiv-2502-11061.creator: Yoav Meiri, Omer Shubi, Cfir Avraham Hadar, Ariel Kreisberg Nitzav Yevgeni Berzak
arxiv-2502-11061.description: Abstract Be it your favorite novel, a newswire article, a cooking recipe or an academic paper -- in many daily situations we read the same text more than once. In this work, we ask whether it is possible to automatically determine whether the reader has previously encountered a text based on their eye movement patterns.

arxiv-2510-03485.title: Towards Policy-Compliant Agents: Learning Efficient Guardrails for Policy Violation Detection
arxiv-2510-03485.creator: Xiaofei Wen, Wenjie Jacky Mo, Yanan Xie, Peng Qi, Muhao Chen
arxiv-2510-03485.description: Abstract Autonomous web agents need to operate under externally imposed or human-specified policies while generating long-horizon trajectories. However, little work has examined whether these trajectories comply with such policies, or whether policy violations persist across different contexts such as domains (e.g., shopping or coding websites) and subdomains (e.g., product search and order management in shopping).

arxiv-2512-02390.title: Error estimates for semi-Lagrangian schemes with higher-order interpolation for conservation laws with dispersive terms
arxiv-2512-02390.creator: Haruki Takemura
arxiv-2512-02390.description: Abstract . We establish error estimates for semi-Lagrangian schemes for the initial value problem of one-dimensional conservation laws with a dispersive term, including the Korteweg–de Vries equation. The schemes considered in this paper are based on the semi-Lagrangian technique combined with spatial discretization by higher-order interpolation operators.

pmc-10595490.title: Maternal healthy lifestyle score and psychological well-being: secondary analyses of the PEARS RCT
pmc-10595490.creator: K Philippe, F M McAuliffe, C M Phillips
pmc-10595490.description: BackgroundThe associations between lifestyle behaviours and well-being are still poorly understood, particularly in the antenatal period when women are potentially exposed to increased stress and anxiety. Moreover, lifestyle behaviours have often been investigated individually, while a Healthy Lifestyle Score (HLS) comprising low-risk protective lifestyle behaviours can be useful for studying links between overall lifestyle and health and psychosocial outcomes.

pmc-10610733.title: Metabolite Profiling in the Liver, Plasma and Milk of Dairy Cows Exposed to Tansy Ragwort (Senecio jacobae) Pyrrolizidine Alkaloids
pmc-10610733.creator: Korinna Huber, Janine Saltzmann, Sven Daenicke
pmc-10610733.description: Background: Plant-derived pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) in feed cause metabolic disturbances in farm animals resulting in high economic losses worldwide. The molecular pathways affected by these PAs in cells and tissues are not yet fully understood. The objective of the study was to examine the dose-dependent effects of orally applied PAs derived from tansy ragwort in midlactation dairy cows.

pmc-11691003.title: PSYCHOMETRICS OF THE PHYSICAL RESILIENCE SCALE IN OLDER ADULTS LIVING WITH DEMENTIA: PROXY RESPONSES
pmc-11691003.creator: Barbara Resnick
pmc-11691003.description: Physical resilience is defined as the ability to recover or optimize function in the face of physical challenges. Physical resilience has been conceptualized as a trait focusing on the way individuals respond to stressors versus an outcome of the stressor(s) or physically challenging experience.

pmc-12503338.title: Histopathological change of age-related hearing loss in female advance-aged CBA/CaJ mice
pmc-12503338.creator: Yoshiaki Inuzuka, Kunio Mizutari, Takaomi Kurioka, Jun Suzuki, Yutaka Koizumi, Koji Araki, Akihiro Shiotani, Miriam A. Hickey, Miriam A. Hickey, Miriam A. Hickey, Miriam A. Hickey, Miriam A. Hickey, Miriam A. Hickey, Miriam A. Hickey
pmc-12503338.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). With the increase in the older population, the number of individuals with age-related hearing loss is also growing explosively. Therefore, there is an urgent need to identify the detailed pathology of age-related hearing loss and develop novel treatment strategies. In this study, we have investigated the audiological physiology and cochlear pathology of advanced-age CBA/CaJ mice, a strain that resists early pathological hearing loss. The subjects were naturally aged close to their lifespan limit (> two years) under normal in vivo conditions.

pmc-12508212.title: Superior colliculus encodes the visual cue associated with rewarding behavior in sucrose self-administration in mice
pmc-12508212.creator: Xingfang Cun, Huimin Zhu, Ning Wu, Manyi Jing, Rui Song
pmc-12508212.description: Associative learning, serve as the neurobiological basis of operant conditioning, is essential for adaptive fitness and survival optimization. The visual cue-guided reward acquisition is fundamental in associative learning. However, the pathological memory formed through excessive reward-associated visual cues is also a critical factor contributing to addictive disorders.

pmc-13339578.title: Using body mapping to explore perceptions of resilience with 7–12‐year‐old Muslim children in East London: A qualitative study
pmc-13339578.creator: Aisling Murray, Imogen I. Hensler, Eleanor Keiller, Faiza Durrani, Patrisiya Ali Taleb, Maria Grazia Turri, Jennifer Y. F. Lau
pmc-13339578.description: BackgroundUnderstanding resilience in pre‐adolescence is important for informing interventions to promote good mental health. Middle childhood is a critical developmental phase, characterised by significant emotional and behavioural development. However, there is limited research on children's perceptions and diverse experiences of resilience which could inform interventions.

pmc-13493791.title: Process-integrated engineered resting cells for biocatalytic production of rare natural sugars from sole methanol molecules
pmc-13493791.creator: Yujie Wang, Guangyu Liu, Feng Gao, Hongwei Zhang, Aobo Chen, Jiangyuan Pan, Wei Xiong, Meng Jiang, Nana Wang, Xiaofeng Cui, Tingting Kong, Chao Gao, Yujie Xiong
pmc-13493791.description: The biocatalytic conversion of green methanol, a promising feedstock, into high value-added products is seen as an attractive way to establish sustainable biomanufacturing. Although natural and engineered microorganisms can utilize methanol, efficiently converting C1 carbon into valuable chemicals in growing cells remains challenging because non-native pathways often suffer from low carbon utilization and limited catalytic stability.
